system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s **[STANDARD]**, “cleared”, “accepted” and “settled” labels do not establish Buyer approval. Review all issues; no Amelia Frost approval has been given for the conditional fallbacks.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m for general Warranty Claims. | 25% / AUD 6m; 20% only with Amelia’s prior written authority identifying the draft. | **Reject; restore 25%.** Matching a fallback does not authorise its use. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, recovering only the excess. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Amend both thresholds and recovery mechanics.** Seller’s formulation materially excludes otherwise recoverable losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notice within 18 months; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | 24 months for general claims; 18 months requires Amelia’s written approval; preserve separate regimes. | **Restore 24 months and remove the blanket extension.** Neither the shorter period nor cross-category application is authorised. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate 100% cap, at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bars. | **Reject general-regime treatment.** Ownership and capacity risks require distinct protection. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims without an express exception. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert overriding carve-outs throughout.** These protections cannot be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Wholesale data-room disclosure, plus Accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Specific fair disclosure; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Replace general deeming with specific fair disclosure.** Mere availability of information must not defeat warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters discoverable from data-room or public records. | Delete blanket actual/constructive Buyer-knowledge exclusions; any retained seller-knowledge qualification must identify named persons and require reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3 as proposed.** It improperly transfers diligence and discoverability risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent, although no final consent or conditions evidence is supplied. | Effective consent **and evidence all associated conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Require a substantive Completion condition and current evidence.** Delivery alone is insufficient for a customer representing approximately 30% of revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release follows Completion; no repayment or final discharge supplied. | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; any deferred release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia’s approval. | **Require the repayment/release package before proceeding.** The proposed unsecured post-Completion promise leaves financing and security risk unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional bonuses treated as Seller’s matter and omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Explicit funds-flow provision or Seller funding for triggered bonuses **plus applicable triggered on-costs**. | **Reconcile conditions, on-costs and funding expressly.** Silent omission can leave Buyer or the Company funding Completion-triggered liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller says adequate; AUD 180,000 recorded open without independent verification. | Broader protection for the Ironquay IP exposure, preserving the SOW3 cure through cleared payment and effective transfer/confirmatory assignment evidence. | **Broaden indemnity and verify payment/title status.** Neither payment nor non-payment of AUD 180,000 is independently established, and payment-only cover may miss IP exposure. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said unlikely material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Preserve logs, investigate access and scope, and require continuing updates; determine legal obligations from evidence. | **Maintain investigation and information covenants without prejudging outcome.** No confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand is established. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate characterised as ordinary-course operating costs; underlying disclosure leaves timing and obligations unclear. | Assess DD-008/DD-011 together for scope, timing, accrual, avoidability and termination rights. | **Reserve classification pending evidence; no automatic Debt treatment or deduction.** Neither Seller’s operating-cost label nor a price adjustment is yet substantiated. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations extend across Claims; title/capacity and Tax/IP drawn into the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories distinct, with express applicable protections and no hidden general override. | **Redraft scope and precedence provisions expressly.** Blanket language could silently erode separately negotiated remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 internal share register said to evidence 100% ownership. | Independent corroboration of title, ownership, absence of encumbrances and authority. | **Require independent verification before Completion.** The supplied internal register is a source, not independent proof. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Seller declares Tax/IP settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax/IP terms open for express negotiation, including their scope and applicable liability treatment. | **Reject the asserted settlement and reserve both categories.** No resolution or unlimited liability should be assumed. |
=== END ADVICE ===
